core_relation.sentence: The resurrection is the central, non-removable linchpin of the Christian message and practice: remove it and the whole gospel, all doctrine, and all practical application collapse.
core_relation.quote: Paul says, 'Remove that one thing and forget all the heavy theology we talk about.' ... If it's not for X, you know, and that X is the resurrection. It gives meaning to the deity, the death, the resurrection, what we call the gospel message. But all of pastoral theology, all of practice [S051][S054][S055][S056]

core_relation_run2.sentence: The resurrection is the necessary, all-or-nothing center of the gospel, theology, practice, and every application of the Christian life; remove it and everything else collapses.
core_relation_run2.quote: Paul says, "Remove that one thing and forget all the heavy theology we talk about." [S005]

product_test.quote: It's everything. Paul says, 'Remove that one thing and forget all the heavy theology we talk about.' [S004][S005] / So you need the resurrection to complete the gospel. [S035] / if Jesus died but does wasn't raised his death was in vain. [S034]
product_test.reason: The paper repeatedly states that removing the resurrection zeroes out the gospel, the cross, all doctrine, and all practice; it is not merely weakened but rendered void. This is the zero-collapse structure of a multiplicative relation.

slots.plays_role: External negentropy influx: the resurrection itself as the outside source that sustains meaning, hope, and coherence in life, especially under suffering and doubt.
slots.quote: if Jesus is raised from the dead, I've got nothing but pain. As bad as that is, I've got nothing but pain to worry about. It doesn't mess with my message. [S232][S233][S234]

slots.plays_role: Alignment: radical commitment and love of God with all heart, soul, strength, and mind; marriage as total mutual belonging.
slots.quote: Love God with all your heart, soul, strength of mind. ... I use the example of um marriage uh when we get married basically we're saying to each other all of me belongs to you. All of you belongs to me. [S081][S078][S079]

slots.plays_role: Signal fidelity: truth that survives transmission, especially the minimal facts argument that the resurrection can be known even if the Bible has errors.
slots.quote: if there are errors in scripture and you think you're going to disprove Christianity, you're barking up the wrong tree. And that's why the minimal facts argument says I can get there without. [S157][S158]

slots.plays_role: Effective entropy: suffering, emotional doubt, fear of death, and sin as the disorder that lowers coherence and is counteracted by resurrection truth.
slots.quote: Emotional doubts by far the most common 70 to 80%. ... what's the for the Christian, what's the what's the counter? It's it's the gospel message is the truth. What's the center of the gospel message? The resurrection. [S240][S250][S251][S252][S253]

slots.plays_role: Temporal integration: time as the arena where resurrection faith is applied repeatedly, questions are lived with, and heaven is awaited.
slots.quote: I can wait for heaven if it means seeing her again, but I'm only going to get there if I stay true to the Lord and I have the resurrection. [S404]

slots.plays_role: Compression: the gospel message compresses to the core formula 'deity, death, resurrection' and the resurrection as the one essential truth.
slots.quote: Deity, death, resurrection. If that's true, whatever you say about the New Testament doesn't stop the gospel message. [S201][S202]

slots.plays_role: Phase transition: the resurrection as the threshold event that changes everything—if true, Christianity is true; if false, the cross means nothing.
slots.quote: And if Jesus rose from the dead, Christianity is true. That's the one evidential point I'd like people want to hear here. If there's a resurrection, Christianity is true. [S203][S204][S205]

slots.plays_role: Superposition: unresolved questions about suffering and God's purposes are held open, with the resurrection as the guarantee that answers exist.
slots.quote: There may be answers, but that doesn't mean Gary Habermass knows the answers. But I can trust God who's omnipotent, omnicient, underpresent, omni, benevolent. [S576][S577]

slots.plays_role: Non-local correlation: communal resurrection—believers are raised together with Christ, and the resurrection connects all doctrines and practices.
slots.quote: He says I'm suffering from these questions but you and I it's communal resurrection. He says you and I will be raised together and sit with Christ in heaven. [S594][S595]

slots.plays_role: Integration: the resurrection as the local integrator inside the product—it is the nexus that ties together deity, death, gospel, pastoral theology, and practice.
slots.quote: All these things are tied together, but the nexus is easily the deity, death, and resurrection. And the nexus of that nexus is the resurrection because Paul said, 'You don't have any of the others without that.' [S039][S040]

one_line: The resurrection functions as the multiplicative linchpin of Christian life and thought, analogous to the master equation's product structure where removing it collapses the whole.
breaks: The paper treats the resurrection as a binary historical fact rather than a continuous variable; the master equation's factors are generally continuous, so the analogy is more discrete than the reference.
The role of G (external negentropy) is not a separate input but is identified with the resurrection itself, collapsing the distinction between source and event.

The paper's 'radical commitment' (M) is said to be a response to grace, not a co-requisite for salvation; this introduces a directional asymmetry not present in the symmetric product of the master equation.
The Holy Spirit is mentioned as an agent but not mapped to a distinct slot, suggesting an extra factor without a clear slot.

The paper treats the resurrection as a single non-negotiable factor, whereas the master equation is a product of ten distinct factors; the paper does not distinguish separate multiplicative components.
The paper's 'radical commitment' (M) is presented as a response to grace, not as a factor that must be non-zero for the gospel to be true; it is more consequence than condition.
The paper does not treat S_eff as a factor that can be zeroed out; suffering is real but not a variable that can collapse the equation.
The paper's logic is more binary (resurrection true/false) than multiplicative across ten slots.
